vars.label: Jobs (all employers)
vars.ref: BLS QCEW, all industries and ownerships
vars.definition: Average number of jobs in the year at employers located in the municipality (wage-and-salary jobs covered by unemployment insurance, which the Bureau says is about 95% of jobs in the United States; self-employed and informal work are not counted). Jobs are counted where the work is done, not where workers live.

vars.label: Private-sector jobs
vars.definition: Average jobs at private employers located in the municipality.

vars.label: Government jobs (federal, state, local)
vars.definition: Total jobs minus private-sector jobs: federal, Commonwealth and municipal government employment (including municipal agencies and public schools).

vars.label: Government share of jobs
vars.definition: Government jobs as a share of all jobs in the municipality.

vars.label: Establishments
vars.definition: Average number of establishments (work sites of employers with employees) located in the municipality.

vars.label: Total wages paid
vars.definition: Total wages paid in the year by employers located in the municipality, in that year's dollars.

vars.label: Average annual pay per job
vars.definition: Total wages divided by average jobs: what the average job at an employer in the municipality pays, in that year's dollars. It describes the jobs located there, not the residents' incomes.

vars.label: Jobs per employed resident
vars.ref: BLS QCEW jobs ÷ ACS employed residents
vars.definition: Jobs located in the municipality divided by employed residents (ACS). Above 1 the municipality is a job centre that draws commuters; well below 1 it is a bedroom community. Informal and self-employed work is in the denominator but not the numerator.

vars.label: Unemployment rate (BLS)
vars.definition: Unemployed people as a share of the labor force, annual average. A Bureau estimate built from local administrative and survey data and controlled to state totals (not a direct count), so it is smoother than a survey of a small municipality could be. The file has no annual average for 2020, and the latest year is preliminary: small municipalities can swing from one year to the next (and be revised).

vars.label: Labor force
vars.definition: Residents 16 and over who are working or looking for work, annual average.

vars.label: Employed residents (BLS)
vars.definition: Labor force minus unemployed, from the BLS labor force and unemployment rate.

vars.label: Unemployed residents (BLS)
vars.definition: Labor force times the unemployment rate.

vars.label: Tourism-related jobs (arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, food)
vars.definition: Private jobs in arts, entertainment and recreation (NAICS 71) and accommodation and food services (72): the usual statistical stand-in for the visitor economy. Includes restaurants that serve residents as much as visitors. Where the Bureau withholds arts, entertainment and recreation for a small municipality, only accommodation and food are counted, so the figure is slightly low there.

vars.label: Accommodation jobs (hotels, inns, rentals)
vars.definition: Private jobs in accommodation (NAICS 721).

vars.label: Food service jobs (restaurants, bars)
vars.definition: Private jobs in food services and drinking places (NAICS 722).

vars.label: Industry concentration (Herfindahl index)
vars.definition: Sum of squared shares of jobs across the private NAICS sectors and government, times 10,000. Lower means a more diversified local economy; 10,000 means all jobs in one sector. Computed only where the published sectors cover at least 80% of jobs.

vars.label: Jobs: Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 11, agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Mining and quarrying
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 21, mining and quarrying, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Utilities
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 22, utilities, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Construction
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 23, construction, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Manufacturing
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 31-33, manufacturing, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Wholesale trade
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 42, wholesale trade, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Retail trade
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 44-45, retail trade, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Transportation and warehousing
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 48-49, transportation and warehousing, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Information
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 51, information, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Finance and insurance
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 52, finance and insurance, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Real estate and rental and leasing
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 53, real estate and rental and leasing, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Professional, scientific and technical services
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 54, professional, scientific and technical services, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Management of companies
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 55, management of companies, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Administrative, support and waste services
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 56, administrative, support and waste services, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Educational services
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 61, educational services, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Health care and social assistance
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 62, health care and social assistance, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Arts, entertainment and recreation
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 71, arts, entertainment and recreation, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Accommodation and food services
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 72, accommodation and food services, at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Jobs: Other services (except public administration)
vars.definition: Average jobs in private-sector NAICS 81, other services (except public administration), at employers located in the municipality. Blank where the Bureau withholds the figure to protect an employer's confidentiality (common in small municipalities).

vars.label: Median household income
vars.definition: Median household income of the residents, in the dollars of the last year of each five-year window.

vars.label: Per capita income
vars.definition: Income per resident, in the dollars of the last year of each five-year window.

vars.label: Median income of owner households
vars.definition: Median household income of owner-occupied households.

vars.label: Median income of renter households
vars.definition: Median household income of renter-occupied households.

vars.label: Population below the poverty level
vars.definition: Share of people whose income in the past 12 months was below the federal poverty level.

vars.label: Income inequality (Gini index)
vars.definition: Gini index of household income: 0 is perfect equality, 1 is one household holding all income.

vars.label: Households earning under $25,000
vars.definition: Share of households with income below $25,000 in the past 12 months (dollars of the window's last year).

vars.label: Households earning $75,000 or more
vars.definition: Share of households with income of $75,000 or more in the past 12 months (dollars of the window's last year).

vars.label: Employment rate, residents 16+ (ACS)
vars.definition: Employed civilians as a share of all residents 16 and over, from the survey. Low in Puerto Rico partly because many adults are retired or outside the formal labor force.

vars.label: Unemployment rate (ACS survey)
vars.definition: Unemployed as a share of the civilian labor force, from the five-year survey (noisier than the BLS series for small municipalities).

vars.label: Adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher
vars.definition: Share of adults 25 and over holding a bachelor's, master's, professional or doctoral degree.

vars.label: Employed residents 16+ (ACS)
vars.definition: Civilian employed residents 16 and over, from the survey.

vars.label: Residents working for government
vars.definition: Employed residents who work for local, Commonwealth or federal government, wherever the job is.

vars.label: Self-employed residents
vars.definition: Employed residents working for themselves (own business, incorporated or not). A rough window on the informal economy, which the jobs data do not see.

vars.label: Residents working for nonprofits
vars.definition: Employed residents who work for private not-for-profit organisations.

vars.label: Workers who drive alone to work
vars.definition: Share of all workers 16 and over (including those who work at home) who usually drive alone to work.

vars.label: Workers who take public transportation to work
vars.definition: Share of all workers 16 and over (including those who work at home) who usually take public transportation (excluding taxis).

vars.label: Workers who walk to work
vars.definition: Share of all workers 16 and over (including those who work at home) who usually walk to work.

vars.label: Workers who work from home
vars.definition: Share of workers 16+ who worked at home.

vars.label: Commutes of 45 minutes or more
vars.definition: Share of commuters (excluding those working at home) whose usual trip to work takes 45 minutes or longer.

vars.label: Households with no vehicle
vars.definition: Share of occupied homes with no vehicle available.

vars.label: Households with an internet subscription
vars.definition: Share of households with any internet subscription. First available in the 2013-2017 window.

vars.label: Households with no internet access
vars.definition: Share of households with no internet access at all. First available in the 2013-2017 window.

vars.label: Federal awards, all types
vars.definition: Dollars of federal contracts, grants, direct payments, loans and other assistance obligated in the federal fiscal year (October to September) for work or benefits in the municipality. Awards to the Commonwealth government for statewide programs are often attributed to the capital, so San Juan is overstated and other municipalities understated. The Puerto Rico figure is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts awards that name no municipality, so the 78 municipalities add up to less than the island.

vars.label: Federal contracts
vars.definition: Federal contract obligations by place of performance, fiscal year.

vars.label: Federal grants
vars.definition: Federal grant obligations by place of performance, fiscal year. Includes disaster-recovery and block grants.

vars.label: Federal direct payments
vars.definition: Federal direct payments to individuals (for example benefit programs) by place of performance, fiscal year.

vars.label: Federal loans (estimated cost to the government)
vars.definition: Estimated subsidy cost to the government of federal loans and loan guarantees (the cost, not the amount lent), by place of performance, fiscal year. It can be negative when earlier estimates are revised.

spend.note: subsidy cost, not the amount lent

vars.label: Federal other assistance
vars.definition: Federal insurance and other assistance not in the categories above.

vars.label: Social Security retirement benefits
vars.definition: Federal obligations for Social Security Retirement Insurance (assistance listing 96.002) by place of performance, federal fiscal year (October to September). Benefits paid to retired workers and their families, placed where the beneficiaries live (the shares match the Social Security Administration's own county tables). The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality.

vars.label: Social Security disability benefits
vars.definition: Federal obligations for Social Security Disability Insurance (assistance listing 96.001) by place of performance, federal fiscal year. Benefits paid to workers who cannot work because of a disability, and their families. The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality.

vars.label: Social Security survivors benefits
vars.definition: Federal obligations for Social Security Survivors Insurance (assistance listing 96.004) by place of performance, federal fiscal year. Benefits paid to the families of workers who have died. The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality.

vars.label: Veterans disability compensation
vars.definition: Federal obligations for Veterans Compensation for Service-Connected Disability (assistance listing 64.109) by place of performance, federal fiscal year. Monthly payments to veterans with a disability caused or made worse by military service. The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality.

vars.label: Pell Grants
vars.definition: Federal obligations for Federal Pell Grants (assistance listing 84.063) by place of performance, federal fiscal year. Grants to low-income undergraduate students, placed at the college or university that receives them, not where the students live, so municipalities with a campus show money and the others show none. The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality.

vars.label: Head Start grants
vars.definition: Federal obligations for Head Start (assistance listing 93.600) by place of performance, federal fiscal year. Grants for early childhood education, placed where the grant recipient (a municipality, a consortium or a nonprofit) reports the work, which can serve children of nearby municipalities too. The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality.

vars.label: Project-Based Rental Assistance
vars.definition: Federal obligations for Section 8 Project-Based Rental Assistance (assistance listing 14.195) by place of performance, federal fiscal year. HUD rent payments to owners of privately owned buildings for units rented to low-income households, placed where the building is. The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance obligated (federal share)
vars.definition: Federal share of FEMA Public Assistance projects (repair of roads, schools, power, water and other public facilities after disasters) by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. A large part is recorded as statewide and cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes it.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: debris removal (federal share)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, damage category A
vars.definition: Federal share obligated for FEMA Public Assistance projects in damage category A (clearing debris from public property and roads), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. Part of fema_pa_obligated: the eight categories add up to it. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: emergency protective measures (federal share)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, damage category B
vars.definition: Federal share obligated for FEMA Public Assistance projects in damage category B (actions to save lives and protect property during and right after the disaster, such as shelters, generators and emergency repairs), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. Part of fema_pa_obligated: the eight categories add up to it. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: roads and bridges (federal share)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, damage category C
vars.definition: Federal share obligated for FEMA Public Assistance projects in damage category C (repair of public roads, bridges and their drainage), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. Part of fema_pa_obligated: the eight categories add up to it. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: water control facilities (federal share)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, damage category D
vars.definition: Federal share obligated for FEMA Public Assistance projects in damage category D (repair of dams, levees, channels and other works that control water), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. Part of fema_pa_obligated: the eight categories add up to it. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: buildings and equipment (federal share)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, damage category E
vars.definition: Federal share obligated for FEMA Public Assistance projects in damage category E (repair or replacement of public buildings, their contents and vehicles), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. Part of fema_pa_obligated: the eight categories add up to it. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: utilities (federal share)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, damage category F
vars.definition: Federal share obligated for FEMA Public Assistance projects in damage category F (repair of power, water, sewer and communication systems), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. Part of fema_pa_obligated: the eight categories add up to it. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: parks, recreation and other (federal share)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, damage category G
vars.definition: Federal share obligated for FEMA Public Assistance projects in damage category G (repair of parks, beaches, recreation sites and other public facilities), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. Part of fema_pa_obligated: the eight categories add up to it. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: management and administrative costs (federal share)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, damage category Z
vars.definition: Federal share obligated for FEMA Public Assistance projects in damage category Z (the costs of managing the grant), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. Part of fema_pa_obligated: the eight categories add up to it. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

vars.label: FEMA Public Assistance: Section 406 mitigation proposed (project cost)
vars.ref: OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects, mitigationAmount
vars.definition: Cost proposed for Section 406 hazard mitigation inside Public Assistance projects (making a repaired facility stronger than before), by applicant municipality and the year of the disaster declaration. It is a project cost, not the federal share, and FEMA warns that some proposals are missing and some values are negative after adjustments. Projects recorded as statewide cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them.

spend.note: project cost, not the federal share

vars.label: FEMA Hazard Mitigation: federal share approved
vars.definition: Federal share of the Hazard Mitigation Assistance subapplications that FEMA approved (HMGP, BRIC, FMA and PDM: projects and plans that reduce future disaster losses), by benefiting municipality and federal fiscal year (for disaster grants, the fiscal year the disaster was declared). A subapplication that benefits several municipalities is split equally among them. Subapplications for the whole island cannot be placed in a municipality; the Puerto Rico value includes them. Approved is not obligated or paid.

vars.label: FEMA Hazard Mitigation: federal money obligated
vars.definition: Federal money FEMA has obligated (made available, in steps as project milestones are met) for Hazard Mitigation Assistance subapplications, by benefiting municipality and federal fiscal year of the grant. Split and placed as for the federal share approved. Money obligated is not money paid.

vars.label: FEMA Hazard Mitigation: federal share awaiting decision
vars.definition: Federal share requested in Hazard Mitigation Assistance subapplications that were sent to FEMA and have no decision yet (status Pending or Submitted to FEMA), by benefiting municipality and federal fiscal year of the grant. Split and placed as for the federal share approved.

vars.label: FEMA Hazard Mitigation: approved subapplications
vars.definition: Number of Hazard Mitigation Assistance subapplications (projects, plans and their management) that FEMA approved, by benefiting municipality and federal fiscal year of the grant. A subapplication that benefits several municipalities counts once in each, so the municipalities add up to more than Puerto Rico; the Puerto Rico value counts each subapplication once.

vars.label: Federal money spent by the municipio government
vars.ref: Federal Audit Clearinghouse, schedule of expenditures of federal awards
vars.definition: Federal awards expended by the municipio government in its fiscal year, from all federal agencies, received directly or through a pass-through entity such as a Commonwealth agency. Loans count the amount used in the year. Money spent, not obligated or awarded. From the single audit the municipio government files with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, municipal fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends). Only the government of the municipio: federal money spent there by Commonwealth agencies, nonprofits, universities or the municipio's own housing projects (which file apart) is not counted. A government that spent less than $750,000 of federal money files no audit ($1,000,000 from FY2026), and a year whose audit is not filed yet is blank. The Puerto Rico value adds up the municipios that filed.

vars.label: Federal money spent by the municipio government: received directly
vars.ref: Federal Audit Clearinghouse, awards marked direct
vars.definition: Part of fac_expended: federal awards the municipio government received straight from a federal agency. From the single audit the municipio government files with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, municipal fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends). Only the government of the municipio: federal money spent there by Commonwealth agencies, nonprofits, universities or the municipio's own housing projects (which file apart) is not counted. A government that spent less than $750,000 of federal money files no audit ($1,000,000 from FY2026), and a year whose audit is not filed yet is blank. The Puerto Rico value adds up the municipios that filed.

vars.label: Federal money spent by the municipio government: through a pass-through entity
vars.ref: Federal Audit Clearinghouse, awards not marked direct
vars.definition: Part of fac_expended: federal awards the municipio government received through a pass-through entity (mostly Commonwealth agencies, such as Vivienda for CDBG-DR). With fac_direct it adds up to fac_expended. From the single audit the municipio government files with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, municipal fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends). Only the government of the municipio: federal money spent there by Commonwealth agencies, nonprofits, universities or the municipio's own housing projects (which file apart) is not counted. A government that spent less than $750,000 of federal money files no audit ($1,000,000 from FY2026), and a year whose audit is not filed yet is blank. The Puerto Rico value adds up the municipios that filed.

vars.label: Federal money spent by the municipio government: Health and Human Services
vars.definition: Part of fac_expended: awards of the US Department of Health and Human Services (mostly Head Start, child care and HIV programs). From the single audit the municipio government files with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, municipal fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends). Only the government of the municipio: federal money spent there by Commonwealth agencies, nonprofits, universities or the municipio's own housing projects (which file apart) is not counted. A government that spent less than $750,000 of federal money files no audit ($1,000,000 from FY2026), and a year whose audit is not filed yet is blank. The Puerto Rico value adds up the municipios that filed.

vars.label: Federal money spent by the municipio government: Housing and Urban Development
vars.definition: Part of fac_expended: awards of the US Department of Housing and Urban Development (mostly housing choice vouchers and community development block grants, CDBG-DR included). From the single audit the municipio government files with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, municipal fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends). Only the government of the municipio: federal money spent there by Commonwealth agencies, nonprofits, universities or the municipio's own housing projects (which file apart) is not counted. A government that spent less than $750,000 of federal money files no audit ($1,000,000 from FY2026), and a year whose audit is not filed yet is blank. The Puerto Rico value adds up the municipios that filed.

vars.label: Federal money spent by the municipio government: Homeland Security (FEMA)
vars.definition: Part of fac_expended: awards of the US Department of Homeland Security, almost all FEMA Public Assistance and Community Disaster Loans. From the single audit the municipio government files with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, municipal fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends). Only the government of the municipio: federal money spent there by Commonwealth agencies, nonprofits, universities or the municipio's own housing projects (which file apart) is not counted. A government that spent less than $750,000 of federal money files no audit ($1,000,000 from FY2026), and a year whose audit is not filed yet is blank. The Puerto Rico value adds up the municipios that filed.

vars.label: Federal money spent by the municipio government: Treasury
vars.definition: Part of fac_expended: awards of the US Department of the Treasury, mostly the COVID-19 Coronavirus Relief Fund and State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds. From the single audit the municipio government files with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, municipal fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends). Only the government of the municipio: federal money spent there by Commonwealth agencies, nonprofits, universities or the municipio's own housing projects (which file apart) is not counted. A government that spent less than $750,000 of federal money files no audit ($1,000,000 from FY2026), and a year whose audit is not filed yet is blank. The Puerto Rico value adds up the municipios that filed.

vars.label: Federal money spent by the municipio government: other agencies
vars.ref: Federal Audit Clearinghouse, other agency prefixes
vars.definition: Part of fac_expended: awards of every other federal agency (Agriculture, Labor, Transportation, Education, Justice and others). The five agency series add up to fac_expended. From the single audit the municipio government files with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, municipal fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends). Only the government of the municipio: federal money spent there by Commonwealth agencies, nonprofits, universities or the municipio's own housing projects (which file apart) is not counted. A government that spent less than $750,000 of federal money files no audit ($1,000,000 from FY2026), and a year whose audit is not filed yet is blank. The Puerto Rico value adds up the municipios that filed.

vars.label: Investment in low-income communities: New Markets Tax Credit (QLICI)
vars.ref: CDFI Fund NMTC public data release, QLICI amount
vars.definition: Dollars of qualified low-income community investments (loans to and equity in businesses and real estate projects in low-income census tracts) that Community Development Entities made with New Markets Tax Credit allocations, in the year each investment was made. From the CDFI Fund's NMTC public data release: each qualified low-income community investment (QLICI) placed in the municipio of its own 2020 census tract (a project with investments in several municipios is counted once, in the municipio of the first one the file lists; none in Puerto Rico does in the 2026 release), in the calendar year the investment was made. A year with no investment in a municipio is 0. The tax credit is 39% of the investment, claimed by the investors over seven years; these are the investments, not the credit.

spend.note: private investment made with a federal tax credit, not federal spending

vars.label: Investment in low-income communities: New Markets Tax Credit projects
vars.ref: CDFI Fund NMTC public data release, projects
vars.definition: Number of projects that received their first New Markets Tax Credit investment that year, counted in the municipio of the project's tract. From the CDFI Fund's NMTC public data release: each qualified low-income community investment (QLICI) placed in the municipio of its own 2020 census tract (a project with investments in several municipios is counted once, in the municipio of the first one the file lists; none in Puerto Rico does in the 2026 release), in the calendar year the investment was made. A year with no investment in a municipio is 0. The tax credit is 39% of the investment, claimed by the investors over seven years; these are the investments, not the credit.

vars.label: FEMA Individual Assistance approved
vars.definition: Dollars approved for owners and renters under FEMA Individual Assistance for disasters declared that year.

vars.label: Households approved for FEMA housing assistance
vars.definition: Owner and renter households approved for FEMA Individual Assistance after a disaster declared that year.

vars.label: Resident population
vars.ref: Census counts and Population Estimates (Housing page series)
vars.definition: Residents: the 2010 and 2020 census counts and the Census Bureau's July 1 estimates for other years. The series steps up in 2020 because 2011-2019 estimates were never revised to the 2020 count.

vars.label: Residents aged 65 and over
vars.ref: Population Estimates, age and sex (Housing page series)
vars.definition: Share of residents 65 or older.

vars.label: Median age
vars.definition: Median age of residents, in years.

vars.label: Type I crimes reported to the Police
vars.ref: Policía de Puerto Rico, Type I crimes by municipality (December report)
vars.definition: Complaints of the eight Type I crimes (murder, rape, human trafficking, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, larceny and vehicle theft) that the Police recorded in the municipality from January to December. Crimes reported, not all crimes committed.

vars.label: Violent Type I crimes (murder, rape, human trafficking, robbery, aggravated assault)
vars.ref: Policía de Puerto Rico, Type I crimes by municipality (December report)
vars.definition: Reported murders, rapes, human trafficking, robberies and aggravated assaults in the calendar year.

vars.label: Property Type I crimes (burglary, larceny, vehicle theft)
vars.ref: Policía de Puerto Rico, Type I crimes by municipality (December report)
vars.definition: Reported burglaries, larcenies and vehicle thefts in the calendar year.

vars.label: Murders (asesinatos)
vars.ref: Policía de Puerto Rico, Type I crimes by municipality (December report)
vars.definition: Murders and non-negligent homicides the Police recorded in the municipality in the calendar year.

deflator.note: CPI-U, US city average, annual average (1982-84 = 100). It is the US index, not a Puerto Rico index.

qcew.name: US Bureau of Labor Statistics — Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW), open-data API
qcew.note: Annual averages 2014 onward for Puerto Rico's municipalities. Cells that would identify one employer are withheld.

laus.name: US Bureau of Labor Statistics — Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS)

acs.name: US Census Bureau — American Community Survey 5-year estimates (summary files)
acs.license: US Government work; cite the Census Bureau as the source
acs.note: Five-year windows labelled by their last year. Dollar values are in the dollars of that last year.

usaspending.name: USAspending.gov — federal awards by place of performance
